newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians call for West Bank, Gaza protests.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians call for West Bank, Gaza protests.

text.p: The Palestinian self-rule Authority called on Tuesday for demonstrations throughout the West Bank, Gaza Strip and Jerusalem to protest against Israel's opening of a tourist tunnel near Islam's third holiest shrine in Jerusalem.

"It will not be a strike but a suspension of work at noon in all Palestinian areas tomorrow in order for there to be marches to demonstrate that the Palestinians will not accept these measures by Israel," Minister of Higher Education Hanan Ashrawi told reporters after an emergency cabinet meeting in Gaza.
The cabinet decision came shortly after the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) called on the U.N. Security Council to reverse Israel's action.

On Tuesday, Palestinians clashed with police after workmen under cover of night and heavy police guard punched a second entrance through a stonewall to a tourist tunnel beside Jerusalem's Temple Mount, a site holy to Jews and Moslems.

Police said they fired rubber bullets to disperse youths throwing stones and bottles and briefly evacuated Jewish worshippers from the Wailing Wall after stones were hurled from the Temple Mount above. Youths also set vehicles alight. Several were arrested and no injuries were reported.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat called the tunnel a "crime" against the religious status quo in the disputed city, and a breach of the foundering Israeli-PLO peace accord.
The 488-metre-long (500-yard) tunnel, which exposes the Herodian foundations of the Wailing Wall, has been open for some time with only one entry and exit point in the Jewish Quarter of the Old City.
"This is a crime, a big crime against our religious and holy places," Arafat said in Palestinian-ruled Gaza. "This (is) Israeli madness to change the features of Jerusalem," he told reporters.

Details about the length of the suspension will be issued later in a statement, officials said. The Higher Islamic Council has already called for a commercial strike in Jerusalem on Wednesday and demonstrations after noon prayers.
In London, visiting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu defended the move.

"(It is) a decision I am very proud that we are implementing," he told reporters on his plane. "Whoever has been in the Wailing Wall tunnel -- I was there a year ago -- could not help but feel the emotion to the depths of his soul...we are touching the rock of our existence," he said.
